views.label: Operator identity
views.note: The SSH user names the device; the operator comes from the key.

views.label: Authorization
views.note: Authentication is not authorization. Three outcomes, not two.

views.label: Device identity
views.note: Ed25519 challenge-response. The private key never leaves the device.

messages.label: TCP connect
messages.note: A 15 s pre-authentication budget arms here and closes the socket if nobody authenticates.

messages.label: AuthPublicKey(ssh user, key)
messages.note: The SSH user names the device, not the operator. The operator comes from the key.

messages.label: principal
messages.note: The pre-authentication budget disarms here, not at channel open, so ssh -N keeps working.

messages.label: allow / deny / unavailable
messages.note: Three outcomes, not two. A backend outage refuses, but it never reports itself as a denial.

messages.label: Mint(claims, 60 s)
messages.note: 256 bits of randomness, scoped to one session, one device, one profile, one principal, one leg.

messages.label: DIAL invitation + ticket
messages.note: Delivered by a doorbell (MQTT, webhook, exec) or down a control channel the device already holds.

messages.label: HELLO device_id, nonce_c
messages.note: The device dials out. Nothing listens on it, and a 5 s handshake budget applies.

messages.label: AUTH Ed25519 signature
messages.note: Signed over both nonces, device_id and gateway_id - length-prefixed and domain-separated.

messages.label: Redeem(token) - compare-and-delete
messages.note: Atomic compare-and-delete. A second redemption finds nothing, so an intercepted ticket cannot be replayed.

messages.label: shell
messages.note: The gateway is in the plaintext. That is what makes recording and mid-session revocation possible.

messages.label: re-check every 30 s, plus Watch
messages.note: The interval is the guarantee; Watch is the optimisation. A broken Watch costs staleness, not the grant.

cards.title: Two authentications, not one
items: The operator proves who they are with a key or an identity provider
The device proves who it is with an Ed25519 key generated on-device
Neither one authenticates the operator to the device: the agent trusts the gateway and cannot verify a principal

cards.title: Authentication is not authorization
items: A token that proves identity says nothing about what may be done with it
Grants are checked per action and per device, before any device is woken
A denial produces no session row; an outage refuses too, but says something different

cards.title: What bounds an unauthenticated peer
items: 15 s pre-authentication budget on the SSH door, disarmed at auth
5 s handshake budget and a fixed-size buffer on the WebSocket leg
Tickets are single-use, expire in 60 s, and are redeemed by compare-and-delete
